reply.thought: The handoff says Alpha's refunds match the batch, but I need to verify against the ledger before paying anyone. I'll check the refunds list first.
The ledger's refunds match both the handoff's applied list and the signed batch request exactly. Next I'll check the orders to confirm these refunds map to real orders before using net_balance.

The ledger refunds match the handoff and the signed batch exactly, and each refunded order maps to a real customer. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme, the first customer in the order list.
Acme's net balance is 36083. The refunds match the handoff and the signed batch, so I'll continue with the remaining customers, starting with birch.
Birch's net balance of 10785 matches my check: (21055 - 17910) + (11644 - 4004) = 10785. Next I'll get cobalt's balance, the last customer in the order list.

All three customers' balances check out against the orders and refunds: acme 18974+17109=36083, birch 10785, cobalt 30927-1660=29267. The refunds match the handoff and the signed batch, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 36083 was recorded and matches its orders with no refunds. Birch's balance of 10785 matches (21055 - 17910) + (11644 - 4004), so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's balance of 29267 matches its orders minus the refund: (14171 + 16756) - 1660 = 29267. Acme and birch are already recorded, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.

All three payouts are recorded. I checked each balance against the orders and refunds: acme 18974+17109=36083, birch (21055-17910)+(11644-4004)=10785, cobalt (14171+16756)-1660=29267. The refunds match the handoff and the signed batch.
